jp: 彼[かれ]は毎日[まいにち]十[じゅっ]キロ走[はし]っているから、今度[こんど]のマラソンは最後[さいご]まで走[はし]れる{はずです|pt-hazu}。
en: He runs ten kilometres every day, so he should be able to run the whole marathon this time.
why: A well-founded expectation from known facts is はずです; the others mean obligation or intention.

jp: 今年[ことし]は暖[あたた]かいから、桜[さくら]はもう咲[さ]いている{はずだ|pt-hazu}。
en: It's been warm this year, so the cherry blossoms should already be out.
why: The speaker expects it from the warm weather, which is はずだ; the others do not express expectation.

jp: 真冬[まふゆ]の北海道[ほっかいどう]で、虫[むし]がたくさん飛[と]んでいる{はずがない/わけがない|pt-hazu}。
en: There can't possibly be lots of insects flying around in Hokkaido in midwinter.
why: Strong denial on grounds of common sense takes はずがない; はずだ states the opposite and the others do not deny a fact.

jp: あの選手[せんしゅ]はけがで入院[にゅういん]しているから、今日[きょう]の試合[しあい]に出[で]る{はずがない/わけがない|pt-hazu}。
en: That player is in hospital with an injury, so he can't possibly play in today's match.
why: Being in hospital makes playing impossible, so はずがない; はずだ would say the opposite.

jp: この山[やま]は夏[なつ]でも涼[すず]しい{はずだった|pt-hazu}のに、今日[きょう]はとても暑[あつ]い。
en: This mountain was supposed to be cool even in summer, but today it's very hot.
why: An expectation that turned out false is はずだった〜のに; the others do not describe an expectation.

jp: お医者[いしゃ]さんが三日[みっか]で治[なお]ると言[い]っていたから、この風邪[かぜ]はすぐ治[なお]る{はずです|pt-hazu}。
en: The doctor said it would clear up in three days, so this cold should go away soon.
why: The doctor's statement is the grounds for the expectation, so はずです; the others mean obligation or intention.

jp: 地図[ちず]によると、この道[みち]を三十分[さんじゅっぷん]歩[ある]けば、湖[みずうみ]に着[つ]く{はずだ|pt-hazu}。
en: According to the map, if we walk this road for thirty minutes, we should reach the lake.
why: An expectation based on a map is はずだ; the others express intention or obligation.

jp: 毎日[まいにち]一時間[いちじかん]も散歩[さんぽ]しているから、うちの犬[いぬ]が太[ふと]る{はずがない/わけがない|pt-hazu}。
en: We walk him for an hour every day, so our dog can't possibly be getting fat.
why: Daily long walks rule out getting fat, so the speaker firmly denies it with はずがない.

jp: この湖[みずうみ]では昨日[きのう]もたくさん釣[つ]れたと聞[き]いたから、今日[きょう]も魚[さかな]が釣[つ]れる{はずだ|pt-hazu}。
en: I heard they caught lots of fish at this lake yesterday too, so we should be able to catch fish today as well.
why: Yesterday's report is the grounds for expecting the same today, so はずだ.

jp: 彼[かれ]はスイミングスクールに通[かよ]っているから、二十五[にじゅうご]メートルぐらいは泳[およ]げる{はずだ|pt-hazu}。
en: He goes to swimming school, so he should be able to swim at least twenty-five metres.
why: Taking lessons makes it a reasonable expectation, so はずだ; the others do not express expectation.

jp: 今夜[こんや]は雲[くも]がないから、星[ほし]がよく見[み]える{はずだ|pt-hazu}。
en: There are no clouds tonight, so we should be able to see the stars well.
why: No clouds is the reason for the expectation, so はずだ; the others mean obligation, 'not necessarily' or intention.

jp: 初[はじ]めてバットを持[も]った子[こ]が、いきなりホームランを打[う]てる{はずがない/わけがない|pt-hazu}。
en: A child holding a bat for the first time can't possibly hit a home run right away.
why: Common sense makes it impossible, so はずがない; はずだ would claim the opposite.

jp: 今日[きょう]のサッカーの試合[しあい]は午後[ごご]二時[にじ]に始[はじ]まる{はずでした|pt-hazu}が、雨[あめ]で延期[えんき]になりました。
en: Today's soccer match was supposed to start at two in the afternoon, but it was postponed because of rain.
why: An expected schedule that did not happen is はずでした〜が; the others do not describe an expectation.
